[DAY1 13:33:30 - DAY1 13:33:59]
I step forward, reach out my hand, and address everyone. "Then put this here. This will be the dessert table," I say. Lucia: "A workbench, a workbench." I watch them, lower my head, and turn my head as I speak. "The workbench and the dessert table are both placed here, right?" I ask. Shure: "No, it's just..." "Yes, it is," I say. "This is a kitchen," I add, nodding and gesturing. "It's all yours," I say. Tasha: "Thank you." Tasha: "It's all open, so if one day..." I pause, then say, "Yes, upstairs is the activity room, here is the meeting room and the kitchen. Makes sense, right?" Shure: "I'll bring a little bit too." Tasha: "Put all the molds into this bag." I turn left, move forward, and place the board eraser and the water on the shelf. Shure: "The coffee machine is going to cost a lot."

[DAY1 13:27:30 - DAY1 13:28:00]
Tasha: "Use paper cups." I pick up a bottle of water, move it, turn right, and walk into the kitchen. I reach into a box and take out two bottles of water, turn left, walk forward, turn right, and set the water down. "Where's the oven?" I ask. Tasha: "By the mixer." I turn my head left and say, "So, where should we put it? Where's the best place to put it?" "Here, this, hmm," I add. Tasha: "Just put it here. I think it should go on top of the oven." Alice: "Peeler." I turn my head right, point at the oven, turn on the tap and drink from the bottle, wave, screw the cap onto the bottle, and then turn right and walk forward. Tasha: "Uh, on top of the microwave would be better." Alice: "On top of the microwave." Shure: "We only have a microwave here." "We bought an oven," I say.

[DAY1 13:29:00 - DAY1 13:29:30]
I walk forward and put things and a board into the kitchen. Katrina: "We're all his assistants." I turn right with my left hand on my forehead, use my other hand to hold my glasses, put my hand down, then turn right and left and set a slider position. "Yeah, we mainly spent a lot here—spent a lot on very useful things." I step forward while speaking, reach out and extend my left hand, then withdraw it and walk toward the whiteboard. "Yeah, just write down the shopping list for the afternoon, or you can write it on this whiteboard—you can all write on this whiteboard now, right? It's pretty easy to write on." Katrina: "I'll get some lemon slices and write it down." Tasha: "Ah, right, I need lemons too." Shure: "Take a picture of the whiteboard." "Take a picture, done."

[DAY1 13:30:30 - DAY1 13:31:00]
Shure: "Oh, no, a bit lower." I stand still and sway slightly. Shure: "Oh, that's not level." I turn right. Alice: "Gloves?" I crouch and unzip the bag. Tasha: "Sterile gloves." Shure: "There aren't many left from the takeout." I step left. "Let's hang it up." Katrina: "If the supermarket has it," I lower my head and turn right. Shure: "It's like three or four bucks." I bend down. Tasha: "Soybean flour." I take items out of my bag and take the oven out of its box. I turn left, set the oven down, and adjust its position. Tasha: "Out of stock, huh?" I move the oven a bit and step back. I turn right. Lucia: "So many ingredients." I stand still. "Oh my."

[DAY1 13:53:30 - DAY1 13:54:00]
I use my phone and look at it. I put it down. Tasha: "Help me write this down." I pick up my phone. Tasha: "Haha, eggs." I turn my head side to side and walk forward, gesturing as I speak. "Are you guys doing it or not?" Shure: "We can cook eggs every morning." I walk to the right and drag the stool into place. Lucia: "Cook them every morning." Tasha: "Hmm, don't we also need sugar?" "Please sit." Alice: "We have powdered sugar but not granulated sugar." Alice: "But I think granulated sugar is actually better." I walk forward while speaking, briefly use my phone, then put it away. Tasha: "Hmm, let's buy some granulated sugar and also a small pack of salt." I stand in front of the kitchen and swing my arms. Tasha: "You can write them together."

[DAY1 13:39:00 - DAY1 13:39:30]
I lean forward. Lucia asks, "The one for sprinkling powdered sugar, right?" I move the oven and set it down, holding and fiddling with it. Shure asks, "I, do you want a chicken burger or a beef burger?" I turn my head left, check my phone, and ask, "Can I have the pizza?" Shure replies, "Sure." Lucia says, "Here's a trash can." I turn my head right and keep holding the oven as I fiddle with it. Shure asks, "Does anyone want a chicken burger?" Tasha says, "Well, I don't want a burger." I fiddle with the oven and say, "Okay, then you can have something else." I ask, "So what do you want to eat? You don't want KFC, right?" Tasha replies, "No, no, I just don't want a burger." I keep tinkering with the oven and say, "Oh, oh, a chicken wrap." Tasha asks, "Do you need help?" Shure says, "One Orleans chicken," and begins another order. I say, "Okay, okay, help me push it in."

[DAY1 13:48:00 - DAY1 13:51:00]
I wrote and erased words on the whiteboard while discussing ideas with Shure and Lucia, noting that “There are 12 now.” We exchanged brief comments on environmental friendliness and the feasibility of using paper cups, with Shure and Lucia concluding that paper cups would not work for our purposes. Afterward, I retrieved my phone to start ordering supplies, consulting Shure and others about necessary items and quantities, including drinks and utensils, confirming leftover utensils would reduce the order. I finalized the order and instructed everyone to wait for the food.

During the ordering process, we discussed drink options, with Lucia suggesting whiskey and tequila as base spirits and favoring a Tequila Sunrise cocktail. I agreed with the group’s evaluation of rum as an alternative to tequila and indicated plans to make two rounds for supplies, relying on the crew if more was needed. Shure planned to check the dorm for additional items the next day.

When Tasha asked about the crew's absence, I explained they were busy attending classes. I handled kitchenware cleanup instructions from Tasha, confirming that utensils and trays needed rinsing or thorough washing as appropriate. I tidied kitchen items by washing and organizing plates, bowls, and utensils, while Lucia and Tasha discussed drink preparations and cleaning procedures. I completed the task by washing my hands and reiterating the cleaning requirements.

[DAY1 13:54:00 - DAY1 13:57:00]
I began by washing dishes and kitchen utensils, using a cloth and sponge under running water, and wiped a pot lid before setting it aside. During this task, the group discussed kitchen supplies, including disposable tableware and an eco-friendly sukiyaki pot. I engaged in the conversation briefly, affirming the eco-friendly aspect before resuming washing.

Tasha reviewed the shopping list aloud, mentioning items such as milk and whipping cream, while Alice suggested using pasteurized eggs for safety, which Tasha and Shure agreed on, noting the benefit of eating raw eggs daily. Tasha continued listing ingredients and potential additions like decorative mint for cocktails and asked about cling film availability. I confirmed with Lucia that some items were missing, and she noted that only utensils like pots and bowls were available. I then resumed washing dishes.

As I cleaned, Tasha detailed more shopping needs including eggs, cornstarch, salt, sugar, milk, whipping cream, and a small pack of milk powder. Shure and Lucia discussed coffee preferences, with Shure wanting coffee powder and asking if it could be used for drinking. Tasha confirmed and inquired if we ground coffee ourselves, to which I responded by shaking my hands. Katrina expressed interest in buying coffee or tea, and I mentioned bringing a unique Singaporean seasoning called coffee duck. Tasha added tart crusts to the list.

I sat down to check the contents of a bag and joined a discussion on which cardboard boxes to keep. Lucia and Alice agreed to retain all cartons for box-making, while we decided to discard any soft or torn boxes. Tasha offered to manage coffee beans, and Alice instructed me to leave the beans in place. I moved into the kitchen as Shure announced plans to restock supplies tomorrow. I mentioned hand-grinding coffee, and Lucia agreed to look into the process. I continued cleaning the pot by hand with a sponge.

Finally, Shure listed other items including a speaker, microphone, coffee, and strawberries. Tasha and Shure noted that strawberries could be stored in the fridge for two to three days. I questioned whether we would consume them within that time, concluding the discussion with a light remark.
